family_title: Gap fill batch 0: representation finetuning (LoReFT), long-context LoRA (LongLoRA), continual-learning LoRA (O-LoRA, InfLoRA), diffusion personalization (Textual Inversion, Custom Diffusion), MoE expert-selective tuning (ESFT), post-hoc LoRA surgery (intruder-dimension reduction)

methods.name: LoReFT
methods.full_name: Low-rank Linear Subspace Representation Finetuning (ReFT family)
methods.paper_title: ReFT: Representation Finetuning for Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \Phi_{\text{LoReFT}}(h)=h+R^{\top}\big(Wh+b-Rh\big)=(I-R^{\top}R)\,h+R^{\top}(Wh+b),\quad R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}\ (RR^{\top}=I_r),\ W\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{r};\ \text{applied to the residual-stream vector } h^{(l)}_i \text{ at the first } p \text{ and last } s \text{ prompt positions of the chosen layers } l\in\mathcal{L};\ \text{LM frozen},\ \{R,W,b\}\ \text{trained};\ \text{DiReFT ablation: } \Phi(h)=h+W_2^{\top}(W_1h+b),\ W_1,W_2\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}
methods.locus: residual-stream hidden states (Transformer block outputs) at a fixed number of prefix and suffix prompt positions in selected layers; generated tokens are not intervened on
methods.structure: Low-rank affine edit of hidden states confined to an r-dimensional subspace. With the orthogonal projector P = R^T R, Phi(h) = (I - P)h + R^T(Wh + b): the component of h in row(R) is replaced by a learned affine function of h, and the orthogonal complement is untouched. The edit is sparse in both positions (prompt prefix and suffix) and layers. DiReFT drops the orthonormality and the difference term, giving a LoRA-shaped map h -> h + W_2^T(W_1 h + b) on activations.
methods.mergeable_reason: The edit acts on the residual stream, including the skip path, at specific token positions, so it cannot be folded into any weight matrix; its cost is a small constant per prompt rather than per generated token.
methods.identity_at_init: Not identity-preserving. In pyreft R gets a random orthogonal initialization (torch orthogonal parametrization) and W, b use the default nn.Linear initialization, so Phi(h) != h at step 0; the identity is recovered only when W = R and b = 0.
methods.key_idea: Learn task-specific interventions on hidden representations instead of changing weights. LoReFT adapts the distributed interchange intervention from causal-abstraction interpretability (DAS): it rewrites the hidden state only inside a learned low-rank orthonormal subspace and only at a few prompt positions, using 15x-65x fewer parameters than LoRA.
methods.results_note: With 0.031% trainable parameters on LLaMA-7B it averages 80.2 on eight commonsense-reasoning tasks, the best among the compared PEFTs. On Llama-2 7B instruction tuning it reaches an 85.60 AlpacaEval win rate with 0.0039% of parameters (LoRA: 81.48). It trails LoRA and adapters on arithmetic reasoning.

relations.note: both edit representations; RED applies a diagonal affine map to FFN outputs at all positions, LoReFT a low-rank subspace edit at selected positions
both are framed as representation interventions; RoAd's is an element-wise 2D rotation that can be merged
DiReFT is essentially LoRA applied to hidden states at chosen positions; LoReFT reports 15x-65x fewer parameters than LoRA
main weight-based baseline on commonsense and arithmetic reasoning
both act only on activations at token positions and leave the weights untouched; prefix-tuning adds key/value states, LoReFT edits existing states

methods.name: LongLoRA
methods.full_name: LongLoRA (LoRA with trainable embeddings and norms, plus Shifted Sparse Attention)
methods.paper_title: LongLoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Long-Context Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W_{\{q,k,v,o\}}=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\ \ (B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}});\ \ E=E_0+\Delta E\ \text{(input embedding, dense)};\ \ \gamma_{\text{norm}}\ \text{(all RMSNorm gains) trained};\ \ \text{training-time attention } \mathrm{S^2\text{-}Attn}:\ \text{tokens split into groups of size } G,\ \text{half of the heads attend within groups, the other half within groups shifted by } G/2;\ \ \text{inference: standard full attention};\ \ \text{RoPE positions rescaled by Position Interpolation};\ \ \text{MLP weights frozen}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted attention matrix } (4L \text{ matrices}) \;+\; |\mathcal{V}|\,d\ \text{(input embedding)} \;+\; (2L+1)\,d\ \text{(norm gains)}
methods.locus: W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o of every attention layer (LoRA, r = 8, alpha = 16 in the official code), plus the input token-embedding matrix and all normalization layers (trained densely); S2-Attn changes only the training-time attention pattern
methods.structure: Composite of three factors. (i) Rank-r additive updates Delta W = BA on the attention projections. (ii) Dense, selective updates of the input-embedding table and the norm gains, which together are under 2% of Llama2-7B's parameters. (iii) A training-only sparsification of the attention graph into block-diagonal token groups, with a G/2 shift on half of the heads so that information flows between neighbouring groups (Swin-style). The paper calls (i)+(ii) 'LoRA+', which is unrelated to LoRA+ by Hayou et al.
methods.mergeable_reason: The LoRA factors merge into W_0, the trained embedding and norm tensors replace the originals, and S2-Attn is used only in training, so inference runs the original dense-attention architecture (with Position-Interpolation RoPE scaling) at the original cost.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA init (B = 0) and the pretrained embedding and norm values, so the weights are unchanged at step 0. The training-time function still differs from the base model, because attention is restricted to shifted local groups and positions are interpolated.
methods.key_idea: Plain LoRA fails at context extension at any rank, but also training the cheap embedding and normalization layers closes almost all of the gap to full fine-tuning. Training can use shifted sparse local attention, which approximates full attention and takes two lines of code, while inference keeps dense attention.
methods.results_note: Extends Llama2 7B, 13B and 70B to 100k, 64k and 32k tokens on a single 8xA100 machine. At 32k context on PG19, LoRA with trainable norms and embeddings reaches perplexity 8.12, versus 8.08 for full fine-tuning and 11.44 for plain rank-8 LoRA.

relations.note: LoRA on W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o, extended with dense updates of the embeddings and norms
trains all normalization gains alongside LoRA; the norms account for the largest single perplexity gain per parameter
both cut fine-tuning compute with training-only sparsity and keep dense inference; LongLoRA sparsifies attention over tokens, SparseLoRA sparsifies channels of the frozen weights

methods.name: O-LoRA
methods.full_name: Orthogonal Low-Rank Adaptation (orthogonal subspace learning for continual learning)
methods.paper_title: Orthogonal Subspace Learning for Language Model Continual Learning
methods.formula_latex: W^{(t)}=W_0+\sum_{i<t}B_iA_i+B_tA_t;\quad \min_{A_t,B_t}\ \mathcal{L}_{\text{task}}(\mathcal{D}_t)+\lambda_1\sum_{i=1}^{t-1}\big\|A_iA_t^{\top}\big\|_F^2\ \big(+\,\lambda_2\,\|(A_t,B_t)\|_2\ \text{in the official code}\big);\quad W_0\ \text{and}\ \{A_i,B_i\}_{i<t}\ \text{frozen},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix per task (after } t \text{ tasks } t\,r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ are stored unless merged)}
methods.locus: W_q and W_v of every attention layer (T5-large, LLaMA-7B)
methods.structure: Sum of per-task rank-r updates. A soft penalty on the cross-Gram matrix A_i A_t^T, which vanishes exactly when the subspaces are orthogonal, pushes the subspaces apart, so Delta W is close to a direct sum of mutually orthogonal rank-r pieces; orthogonality is a regularizer, not a hard constraint. The paper writes the penalty on the left LoRA factor with squared entries; the official code penalizes PEFT's lora_A (the down-projection rows, as written here) with an entry-wise absolute value.
methods.mergeable_reason: Each task's BA is a static low-rank matrix that can be merged into W_0 after training, and inference needs no task ID.
methods.identity_at_init: Each new task's LoRA uses the standard init (B_t = 0), so the model function is unchanged at the start of every task.
methods.key_idea: Use each finished task's LoRA subspace as a cheap stand-in for its gradient subspace, instead of storing gradients as OGD does, and learn the next task's LoRA in a subspace orthogonal to all earlier ones. This gives continual learning without rehearsal or task IDs and preserves instruction-following generalization.
methods.results_note: On the standard 5-task continual-learning benchmark with T5-large, O-LoRA averages 75.8% over three task orders, versus 72.7% for the previous best (LFPT5) and 80.0% for multi-task training. On the 15-task benchmark it averages 69.6% versus 69.2%.

relations.note: one LoRA per task, with earlier LoRAs frozen
O-LoRA uses a soft orthogonality penalty between learned subspaces; InfLoRA uses a hard, data-designed frozen down-projection
both enforce orthogonality to the update subspaces of earlier tasks; OSF does so inside full-rank SVD components
standard LoRA continual-learning baseline that SD-LoRA compares against
both make per-task or per-concept LoRAs orthogonal so their sum does not interfere; O-LoRA uses a penalty during sequential training, Orthogonal Adaptation fixed orthogonal bases for later merging
rehearsal-free continual-learning baseline that uses a prompt pool

methods.name: InfLoRA
methods.paper_title: InfLoRA: Interference-Free Low-Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning
methods.formula_latex: W_t=W_{t-1}+B_tA_t,\quad A_t=(U_t)_{[1:r]}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen, from the SVD } \hat H_t^{\top}=V_t\Sigma_tU_t,\ \ \hat H_t=(I-M_tM_t^{\top})H_t\ \ \text{or}\ \ M_t^{\perp}M_t^{\perp\top}H_t;\quad B_t\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained, init } 0;\quad \Rightarrow\ \Delta_{B_t}W_t=(\Delta_{W}W_t)\,A_t^{\top}A_t,\ \ (B_tA_t)\,M_t=0
methods.trainable_params: r\,d_{out}\ \text{per adapted matrix per task (}A_t\text{ is designed, not trained; one } r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ branch is kept at a time, earlier branches are merged)}
methods.locus: key and value projections of every ViT-B/16 attention block (variant InfLoRA-b5: bottom 5 blocks only)
methods.structure: Rank-r additive update with a frozen, data-designed down-projection A_t. Its orthonormal rows are the top principal directions of the current task's layer inputs H_t after projection onto the orthogonal complement of the old tasks' input subspace span(M_t), which DualGPM maintains; they therefore lie in N_t intersected with M_t-perp. Training B_t alone equals full fine-tuning projected onto row(A_t), Delta W = G A_t^T A_t, so Delta W annihilates old-task inputs. Notation is swapped relative to the paper, which calls the up-projection A_t and the down-projection B_t.
methods.mergeable_reason: After each task the branch B_t A_t is merged into W_{t-1}, and inference uses a single weight matrix without task identity.
methods.identity_at_init: B_t = 0 (zero-initialized up-projection), so the function is unchanged at the start of each task. A_t is set before training by an SVD of the projected current-task activations.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning only the up-projection of a LoRA branch is exactly full fine-tuning restricted to the row space of the frozen down-projection. Choosing that row space inside the new task's input span but orthogonal to the old tasks' input space removes interference by construction.
methods.results_note: With an ImageNet-21K ViT-B/16, InfLoRA reaches 75.65% final accuracy on 10-task ImageNet-R, 86.51% on 10-task CIFAR-100 and 74.53% on 5-task DomainNet, ahead of L2P, DualPrompt, CODA-P, C-LoRA and LAE.

relations.note: one LoRA-like branch per task, merged after training
per task it is structurally LoRA-FA (frozen down-projection, trained up-projection), with a designed rather than random down-projection
hard, data-designed subspace versus O-LoRA's soft orthogonality penalty
SD-LoRA reports 75.26% vs InfLoRA's 69.89% on 20-task ImageNet-R
both restrict continual-learning updates to subspaces orthogonal to what earlier tasks use
prompt-based rehearsal-free class-incremental baseline
prompt-pool baseline

methods.name: Textual Inversion
methods.paper_title: An Image is Worth One Word: Personalizing Text-to-Image Generation using Textual Inversion
methods.formula_latex: v_*=\arg\min_{v\in\mathbb{R}^{d}}\ \mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{E}(x),\,y,\,\epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I),\,t}\Big[\big\|\epsilon-\epsilon_\theta\big(z_t,t,c_\theta(y)\big)\big\|_2^2\Big],\quad y=\text{neutral template (e.g. ``A photo of } S_*\text{'') whose token } S_* \text{ is embedded as } v;\quad c_\theta,\ \epsilon_\theta,\ \mathcal{E}\ \text{and all existing token embeddings frozen}
methods.trainable_params: d\ \ \text{(one token embedding; } k\,d \text{ for a } k\text{-vector pseudo-word)}
methods.locus: token-embedding table of the frozen text encoder (one new row for the pseudo-word S_*); the pseudo-word can appear anywhere in a prompt
methods.structure: Extends the frozen vocabulary with one learned point v_* in input-embedding space. The update is a single new row of the embedding matrix, used compositionally inside arbitrary natural-language prompts rather than as a fixed task prefix.
methods.mergeable_reason: The learned vector is just a new vocabulary entry: inference runs the unchanged text encoder and diffusion model at the same cost, with one token standing in for a word.
methods.identity_at_init: The model itself is untouched. v is initialized to the embedding of a single-word coarse descriptor (e.g. 'cat', 'sculpture'), so prompts without S_* behave exactly as before and S_* starts out as that word.
methods.key_idea: Personalize a frozen text-to-image model by inverting 3-5 images into a new word in its text-embedding space, trained with the ordinary denoising loss. One word embedding is enough to capture an object or style, which can then be composed into new prompts.
methods.results_note: On LDM a single learned embedding reproduces object and style concepts from 3-5 images more faithfully than human-written captions or DALL-E 2 image prompts. CLIP-based and user-study evaluations place it at a favourable point on the reconstruction-editability trade-off, which the learning rate can shift.

relations.note: same frozen-model soft-token principle; a single reusable pseudo-word placed anywhere in a prompt instead of a fixed task prefix
equivalent to training only the embedding row of one newly added token in the text encoder
Custom Diffusion also trains a new token (V*), together with the cross-attention K/V weights
alternative personalization of text-to-image models

methods.name: Custom Diffusion
methods.full_name: Custom Diffusion (cross-attention K/V fine-tuning for multi-concept customization)
methods.formula_latex: K=W^{k}c,\ V=W^{v}c\ \text{in every U-Net cross-attention layer};\quad W^{k}=W^{k}_0+\Delta W^{k},\ W^{v}=W^{v}_0+\Delta W^{v}\ \text{(dense)},\ \text{plus a new modifier-token embedding } V^{*};\ \text{all other weights frozen; loss: denoising loss on the target images plus 200 retrieved real regularization images};\quad \text{merging } N \text{ concepts: } \hat W=\arg\min_W\|WC_{\text{reg}}^{\top}-W_0C_{\text{reg}}^{\top}\|_F\ \ \text{s.t.}\ \ WC^{\top}=V_{\text{tgt}},\ \ \hat W=W_0+\mathbf{v}^{\top}\mathbf{d},\ \ \mathbf{d}=C(C_{\text{reg}}^{\top}C_{\text{reg}})^{-1},\ \ \mathbf{v}^{\top}=(V_{\text{tgt}}-W_0C^{\top})(\mathbf{d}C^{\top})^{-1}
methods.trainable_params: 2\,d_{out}\,d_{text}\ \text{per cross-attention layer } (W^{k},W^{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{text}}) \;+\; d_{text}\ \text{per modifier token}
methods.locus: key and value projections of the text features in all cross-attention layers of the diffusion U-Net (Stable Diffusion), plus the modifier-token embedding
methods.structure: Block mask over the parameter tensors: only the two matrices that read the text condition (W^k, W^v) are updated, densely. Multi-concept merging is a closed-form, equality-constrained least-squares projection: it maps each concept's target-word features to the fine-tuned values while staying close to W_0 on about 1000 regularization captions.
methods.mergeable_reason: The fine-tuned W^k and W^v replace the originals and V^* is one extra vocabulary row, so inference runs the original architecture at the original cost; the closed-form merge folds several concepts into a single pair of matrices.
methods.identity_at_init: Training starts from the pretrained W^k, W^v (Delta W = 0), and V^* is initialized to a rarely occurring token's embedding, so the model is initially unchanged on ordinary prompts.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning moves the cross-attention weights much more than any others, so update only the K/V projections that map text into latent features, together with a learned modifier token and retrieved real images as regularization. The method is fast, small and resists language drift, and concepts can be combined by joint training or a closed-form constrained merge.
methods.results_note: On Stable Diffusion it beats Textual Inversion and matches or beats DreamBooth on text/image alignment and human preference, while training about 5x faster (~6 minutes) and storing 75MB instead of 3GB per concept. The closed-form multi-concept merge takes about 2 seconds.

relations.note: also trains a new token embedding V* jointly with W^k and W^v
both merge linear layers in closed form by least squares on input features; Custom Diffusion adds hard equality constraints on the concepts' target-word features
the paper reports that the K/V updates are effectively low-rank (5x SVD compression with similar quality), though training them as low-rank directly was worse
compact diffusion personalization that also supports multi-concept generation
multi-concept customization by merging per-concept adapters
merging independently trained subject and style adapters

methods.name: ESFT
methods.paper_title: Let the Expert Stick to His Last: Expert-Specialized Fine-Tuning for Sparse Architectural Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: g_i^{l}=\frac{1}{N_s}\sum_{j=1}^{N_s}\frac{1}{L_j}\sum_{k=1}^{L_j}g_{i,k}^{l}\ \ (\text{ESFT-Gate})\quad\text{or}\quad r_i^{l}=\frac{1}{N_s}\sum_{j=1}^{N_s}\frac{1}{L_j}\sum_{k=1}^{L_j}\frac{\mathbb{1}(g_{i,k}^{l}>0)}{K}\ \ (\text{ESFT-Token});\quad E_s^{l}=\text{top-scored experts with }\textstyle\sum_{i\in E_s^{l}}R_i^{l}\ge p;\quad \theta_e\ (e\in E_s^{l})\ \text{trained; all other routed experts, shared experts, attention, router and embeddings frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \sum_{l=1}^{L}|E_s^{l}|\cdot 3\,d\,d_{ff}^{(e)}\ \ (\text{gate/up/down projections of each selected routed expert; on average 2-15 of 66 experts per layer})
methods.locus: the routed (non-shared) FFN experts in each MoE layer that are most relevant to the task; attention, router, shared experts and embeddings stay frozen
methods.structure: Data-dependent block mask over experts. In each layer the selected set is the smallest group of top-scored routed experts whose cumulative relevance (average gate score or token-selection ratio on sampled task data) reaches p. Selected experts are updated densely, everything else is frozen, and routing stays free during training and inference.
methods.mergeable_reason: The updated experts simply replace the originals, so the architecture, routing and inference cost are unchanged.
methods.identity_at_init: Training starts from the pretrained weights (Delta W = 0); expert selection is computed from router statistics on a task sample.
methods.key_idea: In fine-grained MoE LLMs, each task activates a concentrated and distinct set of experts, so fine-tune only the experts most relevant to the task. This nearly matches full fine-tuning on the target task, forgets less, and cuts storage by up to 90%.
methods.results_note: On DeepSeek-V2-Lite, ESFT-Gate averages 50.2 on downstream tasks (FFT 51.0, LoRA 44.9) while keeping more general ability (ESFT-Token 61.5 vs FFT 58.8 and LoRA 59.1), with 2.57-3.20 GB of trained parameters versus 28.6 GB for FFT.

relations.note: main PEFT baseline (rank 8); ESFT beats it on both task performance and general-ability retention
block-level selective tuning placed where the task lives; ESFT chooses experts from router statistics instead of choosing layers
selective full-parameter tuning of a subset of blocks (layers rather than experts)

methods.name: Intruder-dimension reduction
methods.full_name: Intruder Dimension Reduction (post-hoc spectral surgery on LoRA adapters)
methods.paper_title: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: An Illusion of Equivalence
methods.formula_latex: W_0+\Delta W=U\Sigma V^{\top},\ \ W_0=U^{0}\Sigma^{0}V^{0\top};\quad \mathcal{I}=\{\,j\le k:\ \max_i|\langle u_j,u^{0}_i\rangle|<\epsilon\,\};\quad W'=W_0+\Delta W+(\lambda-1)\sum_{j\in\mathcal{I}}\sigma_j\,u_jv_j^{\top};\quad (B',A')=\text{rank-}r\ \text{truncated SVD of } (W'-W_0)\big/\tfrac{\alpha}{r};\quad \text{no training: } W_0 \text{ frozen, the trained } (B,A) \text{ replaced by } (B',A')
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \ (\text{training-free; the output is again a rank-}r\text{ adapter with } r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ parameters per matrix})
methods.locus: every LoRA-adapted linear (or embedding) layer of an already trained adapter
methods.structure: Spectral endomorphism on the space of trained adapters. Among the top-k singular directions of the merged matrix, those nearly orthogonal to every pretrained left singular vector (the intruders) are shrunk by lambda, and the edited Delta W is projected back to rank r. The paper scales only the top intruder per matrix and does not re-project; HF PEFT scales every detected intruder and re-factorizes to rank r.
methods.mergeable_reason: The result is an ordinary LoRA adapter (B', A') that merges into W_0 like any other LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (post-hoc edit). lambda = 1 leaves the adapter unchanged up to rank-r truncation, lambda = 0 removes the intruder components, and lambda > 1 amplifies them.
methods.key_idea: LoRA creates high-ranking intruder singular vectors that are nearly orthogonal to the pretrained spectrum; full fine-tuning does not. These directions drive most of the forgetting, so shrinking them after training recovers pretrained behaviour at little cost in task accuracy.
methods.results_note: Scaling the top intruder dimension of each matrix with lambda = 0.7 (RoBERTa-base on QQP, LoRA r = 8) left test accuracy unchanged and cut fine-tuning-induced forgetting (pre-training loss) by 33.2%. For LLaMA2-7B on MetaMath (r = 256), lambda = 0.3 cost 0.1% accuracy and cut forgetting by 33.3%.

relations.note: post-hoc edit of a trained LoRA adapter, returning a LoRA adapter of the same rank
a preventive alternative: train in the minor singular directions so the principal spectrum is not disturbed; intruder reduction is a post-hoc repair
knowledge-preserving initialization versus post-hoc removal of the components that cause forgetting
the paper finds that PiSSA, which edits principal singular vectors, also produces many intruder dimensions

papers.title: Gradient Projection Memory for Continual Learning
papers.claim: A layer's gradient updates lie in the span of its inputs. GPM stores per-layer orthonormal bases of the old tasks' representation subspaces, found by SVD of activations, and steps orthogonally to them, which causes little or no interference with past tasks and needs no replay.
papers.relevance: This input-space orthogonality is the mechanism InfLoRA builds into a LoRA down-projection (through DualGPM) and that O-LoRA approximates with LoRA subspaces. Categorically, each task's update is a morphism required to vanish on a sub-object (the old tasks' input subspace), which makes continual-learning PEFT a kernel condition.

papers.title: Orthogonal Gradient Descent for Continual Learning
papers.claim: Projecting new-task gradients onto the subspace in which the network's outputs on previous tasks stay unchanged mitigates catastrophic forgetting without storing data, but it does require storing gradient directions.
papers.relevance: Direct ancestor of O-LoRA, which replaces OGD's stored gradients with the LoRA subspaces of earlier tasks; in this sense O-LoRA is OGD transported into the low-rank adapter parameterization.

papers.title: Finding Alignments Between Interpretable Causal Variables and Distributed Neural Representations
papers.claim: Distributed alignment search (DAS) learns, by gradient descent, an orthonormal (rotated) subspace of a hidden representation in which interchange interventions realize a high-level causal variable. This replaces brute-force alignment search and allows distributed, non-neuron-aligned representations.
papers.relevance: LoReFT is DAS's interchange intervention with the counterfactual source replaced by a learned affine map (R s -> W h + b). This links PEFT to causal abstraction: a ReFT is an endomorphism of the hidden-state space that acts only on one sub-object.

papers.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
papers.claim: On a large benchmark for concept steering and detection (Gemma-2-2B/9B), prompting outperforms every representation-based steering method, with finetuning second; difference-in-means is best for detection, and SAEs are not competitive on either task. A rank-1 representation finetuning (ReFT-r1) is competitive on both.
papers.relevance: Gives a sober empirical calibration of intervention-based (activation-editing) adaptation against prompts and weight finetuning, which is useful for placing the ReFT family next to input-augmentation and weight-update PEFT.

papers.title: Representation Engineering: A Top-Down Approach to AI Transparency
papers.claim: Population-level representations, rather than individual neurons or circuits, can be read out and manipulated to monitor and control high-level behaviours of LLMs such as honesty and harmlessness, using simple training-free reading vectors and representation-control operators.
papers.relevance: Training-free activation steering is the zero-training limit of representation interventions, and ReFT is its learned, task-supervised counterpart; the ReFT paper explicitly recasts RepE's operators as parametrizations of its intervention function.

notes: All 8 seeds exist, are distinct from the classic methods already in the catalog, and were kept, one entry each, with no extra methods (this was a fixed-scope gap batch). Formulas were checked against each paper's method section in the arXiv HTML full text and, where relevant, against official code (pyreft interventions.py, the O-LoRA trainer, LongLoRA fine-tune.py, HF PEFT intruders.py). Placement suggestions: (1) loreft: modification_kind input-or-activation-augmentation, not mergeable, not identity at init. It fits a new 'representation / activation-editing' family together with red and road (multiplicative.json already points at the id 'loreft'). DiReFT is described inside the LoReFT entry rather than given its own entry. ReFT is not in HF PEFT as of v0.21.1 (2026-09-29); it ships in pyreft. (2) longlora: hybrid, family lora-core. The paper calls 'LoRA + trainable embeddings and norms' LoRA+, a name clash with LoRA+ (Hayou et al.). In HF PEFT it can be approximated with LoraConfig(target_modules=q,k,v,o, modules_to_save=[embed_tokens, norms]) plus an S2-Attn patch, but it is not a native method, so hf_peft = false. (3) o-lora and inflora: continual-learning LoRA (frontier/composition); hf-peft.json's osf already points at 'o-lora'. O-LoRA's paper writes the orthogonality penalty on the left (up-projection) factor with squared entries, while the official code penalizes PEFT lora_A (down-projection rows) with absolute values and adds an L2 term (lambda_2); the formula follows the code side and the discrepancy is noted in the entry. InfLoRA's paper uses swapped letter names (its A_t is the up-projection, its B_t the frozen down-projection); the entry is rewritten in catalog notation (A = down, B = up). (4) textual-inversion is in diffusers (textual_inversion.py, load_textual_inversion), not in HF PEFT; HF PEFT TrainableTokensConfig applied to a newly added text-encoder token reproduces it, hence the special-case-of edge. (5) custom-diffusion: selective, with a composition edge (closed-form constrained least-squares merge, related to regmean); in diffusers examples/custom_diffusion. (6) esft: selective at expert granularity for MoE LLMs and validated only on DeepSeek-V2-Lite (the paper names this limitation); per-expert parameter count 3 d d_ff^(e) assumes SwiGLU experts. (7) intruder-dimension-reduction: HF PEFT utility since v0.19.0 (2026-04-14), peft.tuners.lora.intruders.reduce_intruder_dimension.
